enrichment.short_title: Unlawful ECRC disclosure of discontinued indecent exposure allegations
key_facts: An anonymised social worker with no criminal convictions sought judicial review of a decision to include non-conviction information on an Enhanced Criminal Record Certificate.
The Other Relevant Information related to two alleged indecent exposure incidents; charges were discontinued after the alleged victim failed to identify the claimant in a covert parade.
The Deputy Chief Constable decided to provide the information to a potential employer via the Criminal Records Bureau without giving the claimant an opportunity to make representations.
The claimant had been dismissed from agency social work employment after the allegations surfaced.
enrichment.procedural_posture: Judicial review of the Chief Constable's decision to provide non-conviction information for inclusion on an ECRC under section 115 of the Police Act 1997.
enrichment.outcome: Decision quashed; declaration that the ECRC information was unlawfully provided; permission to appeal refused (renewable to the Court of Appeal).
enrichment.ratio: Police disclosure of non-conviction information on an ECRC must satisfy Article 8 and common-law requirements of pressing social need and procedural fairness, including an opportunity for the subject to make representations; those standards apply with particular stringency where there has been no conviction and identity or guilt remains in issue.
legal_issues: Whether disclosure met Article 8 and common-law substantive criteria
Whether the disclosure process was procedurally fair
Whether retention and disclosure breached the ACPO Data Protection Code of Practice

notes: Straightforward valuation tribunal appeal on council tax student discount definition.

enrichment.short_title: Council tax student discount and full-time course attendance weeks
key_facts: Mrs Evans undertook an All Wales Part-Time Occupational Therapy degree while seeking a council tax student disregard discount.
Carmarthenshire County Council refused the discount; the West Wales Valuation Tribunal allowed her appeal.
The council appealed on the ground that the course did not require attendance for at least 24 weeks per academic year.
The course brochure showed 43 attendance days and weekly totals below 24 weeks in most years; a programme manager's letter was misread as requiring 33 weeks' attendance.
enrichment.procedural_posture: Appeal to the High Court from a valuation tribunal decision on a council tax student disregard discount.
enrichment.outcome: Appeal allowed; tribunal decision quashed and remitted to a differently constituted panel.
enrichment.ratio: A part-time course qualifies as a full-time course of education under the 1992 Order only if it meets all limbs of the definition, including attendance for at least 24 weeks per year; a tribunal errs in law if it treats a letter about equivalent study hours as proof of a 24-week attendance requirement and wrongly finds the billing authority did not dispute that point.
legal_issues: Whether Mrs Evans's course was a full-time course of education
Whether paragraph 4(1)(b) of Schedule 1 to the 1992 Order was satisfied
Whether the tribunal misinterpreted the programme manager's letter

notes: Asylum state protection point following Gardi and Saber.

enrichment.short_title: Asylum appeal leave and PUK state protection in northern Iraq
key_facts: An Iraqi Kurd claimant alleged persecution by the Islamic Movement in PUK-controlled northern Iraq after supporting the PUK.
An adjudicator accepted much of his account but found the PUK could and would protect him; the IAT refused leave to appeal.
Subsequent Court of Appeal and Court of Session authority cast doubt on treating the Kurdish autonomous region as an entity capable of providing Convention protection.
Circumstances in Iraq had changed materially since the adjudicator's decision.
enrichment.procedural_posture: Judicial review of the Immigration Appeal Tribunal's refusal to grant leave to appeal against an adjudicator's asylum decision.
enrichment.outcome: Application allowed; IAT decision quashed and remitted; permission to appeal granted on the Gardi state protection point.
enrichment.ratio: Where persuasive appellate authority indicates a real prospect that protection from a non-state entity such as the PUK cannot satisfy the Refugee Convention protection test, an IAT decision refusing leave to appeal may be irrational; changed country conditions do not deprive a claimant of access to an independent tribunal if no fresh-claim assurance is given.
legal_issues: Whether the IAT could reasonably conclude there was no real prospect of success
Whether PUK protection qualifies as state or Convention protection
Whether the claim had become academic because of changed circumstances in Iraq
linked_authorities: Saber v Secretary of State for the Home Department

notes: Section 288 planning challenge on Chiswick town houses.

enrichment.short_title: Planning appeal privacy standard and internal facing windows
key_facts: An inspector allowed Wexford Resources' appeal and granted planning permission for four town houses in Chiswick.
A neighbouring resident challenged the decision under section 288 on privacy, design, and outlook grounds.
The scheme placed rear bedroom windows of the same dwelling about 3–4 metres apart across a recess.
Appendix 2 of the Hounslow UDP recommended at least 21 metres between directly facing habitable room windows.
enrichment.procedural_posture: Section 288 application to quash a planning inspector's decision granting permission on appeal.
enrichment.outcome: Application dismissed; all three grounds of challenge failed.
enrichment.ratio: A local plan privacy spacing standard directed at spacing between buildings applies to neighbouring properties, not to facing windows within the same dwelling; an inspector need address only principal important controversial issues and is entitled to proceed on site inspection and existing plans without further evidence unless Wednesbury unreasonableness is shown.
legal_issues: Whether the 21 metre UDP standard applied to internal facing windows within one dwelling
Whether the inspector failed to consider SPG design guidance on habitable rooms overlooking the street
Whether the inspector lacked sufficient evidence on outlook and open aspect
linked_authorities: Bolton MDC v Secretary of State for the Environment
Newsmith Stainless Ltd v Secretary of State for Environment, Transport and the Regions

notes: Renewed permission application in cattle-on-road negligence claim.

enrichment.short_title: Farmer's gate duty after cattle strayed onto road
key_facts: Cattle escaped through an upper-field gate left open by walkers, crossed unfenced land, and walked along a main road.
Mr Donaldson was seriously injured when his motorcycle collided with the cattle.
The county court recorder found Mr Wilson negligent for failing to take inexpensive steps such as a self-closing gate.
Insurers sought permission to appeal because of potential implications for farmers' standards of care.
enrichment.procedural_posture: Renewed application to the Court of Appeal for permission to appeal a county court liability judgment.
enrichment.outcome: Permission granted on condition the defendant indemnifies the claimant for Court of Appeal costs in any event; extended time to serve notice of appeal.
enrichment.ratio: On the particular facts a farmer may owe a duty of care to road users to secure a gate where cattle straying onto a road was foreseeable and inexpensive preventive steps were available; permission may nonetheless be granted where insurers show a compelling reason despite no real prospect of success, subject to appropriate costs conditions.
legal_issues: Whether the recorder was entitled to find negligence on the facts
Whether permission to appeal should be granted for wider industry significance
Appropriate costs conditions for conditional permission

enrichment.short_title: Harassment injunction against SHAC over Yamanouchi landlord
key_facts: Emerson Group companies leased offices to Yamanouchi, a customer of Huntingdon Life Sciences.
Directors and employees received threatening Animal Rights Militia letters demanding Yamanouchi's eviction.
Employee homes and vehicles were damaged and campaign claims appeared on activist websites.
SHAC organisers Greg Avery, Natasha Avery, and Heather James had prior convictions for related campaign conduct.

notes: GMC erasure appeal substituted with suspension.

enrichment.short_title: GMC erasure reduced to suspension for prescription fraud

statutes_considered.title: National Health Service Reform and Health Care Professions Act 2002

key_facts: Dr Abrahaem admitted removing NHS prescription forms and using them to obtain routine medications in false patient names for his family in Egypt.
Police found unused prescription forms, morphine sulphate, and other drugs at his hospital accommodation.
The GMC Professional Conduct Committee ordered erasure from the medical register.
The doctor had otherwise good clinical testimonials but limited insight into the gravity of his misconduct.
enrichment.procedural_posture: Appeal by way of rehearing under section 40 of the Medical Act 1983 against GMC erasure.
enrichment.outcome: Appeal allowed; erasure substituted with immediate suspension for 12 months.
enrichment.ratio: Although persistent prescription fraud and possession of controlled drugs can warrant erasure, the High Court may substitute a lesser sanction where the accepted facts show no patient harm, the doctor remains otherwise fit to practise, and a proportionate suspension can protect public confidence while allowing scope to develop proper professional insight.
legal_issues: Whether erasure was excessive and disproportionate
Whether the PCC took irrelevant considerations into account
Appropriate deference to a professional tribunal on sanction
Impact of Article 1 Protocol 1 on erasure

notes: JR refused where contractual arbitration was available.

enrichment.short_title: Legal aid contract termination and arbitration bar to JR
key_facts: The Legal Services Commission terminated a firm's General Civil Contract and Specialist Quality Mark after a failed pre-contract management audit.
The Contract Review Board upheld termination; the firm gave notice of intention to arbitrate under the contract.
The firm later sought judicial review, including arguments on proportionality and procedural fairness.
Pitchford J had refused permission on the papers on the basis that arbitration was the appropriate route.
enrichment.procedural_posture: Renewed application for permission to apply for judicial review of an LSC Contract Review Board decision.
enrichment.outcome: Permission refused; judicial review not an appropriate substitute for contractual arbitration.
enrichment.ratio: Even where a public-body contract decision may in principle be amenable to judicial review, JR is a remedy of last resort where the parties agreed to final arbitration under the contract; proportionality and fairness complaints tied to the merits are suitable for arbitration and do not justify bypassing that agreed process.

notes: Liability trial on Project Jockey cost-sharing agreement.

enrichment.short_title: Failed MBO cost contribution and technical failure clause
key_facts: Granville Baird fund managers and a management team agreed a 65/35 cost-sharing arrangement for Project Jockey, a management buy-out of Professional Staff Plc.
First Saddle's offer lapsed after about 83% acceptances because Lord Ashcroft held a blocking stake and banks required 90%.
The board voted not to extend the offer after Lord Hodgson's enquiry to Lord Ashcroft.
The claimants sought 35% of residual costs as a technical failure; defendants argued GBCP withdrew without cause.
enrichment.procedural_posture: Trial of liability on whether defendants must contribute 35% of failed takeover costs under a July 2000 cost-sharing agreement.
enrichment.outcome: Judgment for the claimants on liability; failure classified as technical failure triggering the 35% contribution.
enrichment.ratio: Under the agreed cost-sharing scenarios, inability to reach 90% acceptances after the offer was made is a technical failure by First Saddle rather than a GBCP withdrawal without cause; a board decision not to extend the offer, made by independent directors exercising fiduciary judgment, does not convert that failure into a funder withdrawal.
legal_issues: Construction of 'technical failure' versus 'GBCP withdraw - without cause'
Whether the claimants effectively decided not to proceed
Whether independent directors merely followed the claimants' lead
Whether a higher revised offer fell outside the agreement

notes: Ancient JR refused as academic under section 70A.

enrichment.short_title: Academic challenge to declining repetitive planning application
key_facts: Meritgold sought permission to retain a fourth-storey flat built in breach of earlier permission for a three-storey block of six flats.
In April 1999 Barnet declined to determine a January 1999 application under section 70A as substantially the same as an appeal dismissed in June 1998.
Later 2001 and 2003 applications were determined and refused on appeal, addressing revised proposals.
The 1999 judicial review was repeatedly adjourned and heard years later without substantive claimant instructions.
enrichment.procedural_posture: Judicial review of a local planning authority's decision to decline to determine a planning application under section 70A.
enrichment.outcome: Application refused as academic; claimant ordered to pay costs summarily assessed at £4,000.
enrichment.ratio: A section 70A decision not to determine a repetitive application will not be reopened where later determined applications have superseded the dispute and the original challenge has become pointless; even absent academicity, similarity of proposals is a matter of planning judgment for the authority.
legal_issues: Whether the 1999 application was the same or substantially the same as the refused 1998 application
Whether declining to determine was Wednesbury unreasonable
Whether the claim had become academic
